# Coordinated nonradial descent of the exact binary critical budget

For every n>=2, the source in
candidate 4e0a45efacd4af50
admits arbitrarily small actual nonradial deformations that preserve
all its original cap planes, decrease the three core cap masses,
leave every regular cap mass unchanged, and strictly decrease its
TRUE maximal normalized depth. The original inclusion-minimal cap
cover remains inclusion-minimal. No independent copies of shared
originals or free-fiber compatibility assumption are used.

The absolute maximal depth remains exactly B throughout this path.
The decrease in normalized depth comes from a strictly increasing
total mass, with a matching upper and lower certificate for the
absolute depth. This is not an inference from selected budget
decrease alone.

## 1. Fixed data and a compatible core deformation

Use the exact binary base polytope Q and all the original cap planes
from the cited embedding. Write

    Gamma=4/9, t0=1/10, M0=42/25, B=6811/8910,
    Nreg=2^n-2, rho^2=6811/1980.

Keep every regular fiber rho K fixed. On the three core bases use

    L(t) A_t, L(t) D_t, L(t) B_t,
    A_t=(I+tJ)K, B_t=(I-tJ)K, D_t=(A_t+B_t)/2,

where 0<t<t0 is close to t0. The archived exact unrotation proof is
coordinated-unrotation-escapes-the-rotated-triangle-radial-trap.md.
Its core mass and common canonical cap mass are

    M(t)=3(1+t+2t^2)/2,
    D(t)=(6+7t+12t^2-9t^3)/(9(1-t^2)).                  (1)

Put R(t)=D(t)/M(t), and choose

    q(t)=[M0/M(t)+B/D(t)]/2,   L(t)=sqrt(q(t)).         (2)

The cited proof establishes R'(t)>0 on 0<t<1/3, with exact
positive derivative numerator

    1+4t(3-t)+44t^3+9t^4(5-2t^2)+48t^5.

Consequently

    Mcore_new=qM=M0/2+B/(2R(t)) > M0,
    Bcore_new=qD=M0 R(t)/2+B/2 < B.                    (3)

Both changes are strict at first order in t0-t, and L(t0)=1.
The convex hull of the new generators has exactly the intended
integer fibers: binary b again forces the same b in every convex
representation; on b=0 the middle is the exact Minkowski average;
at every other binary b only the two exposed z endpoints occur.
Thus no hidden integer fiber is enlarged. The body stays full
dimensional. Its equality midpoint constraint is preserved exactly.

## 2. Every original plane and every selected budget

Retain the core caps l_i(x)>=2 sum b_j and every regular cap
l_i(x)>=2 ell_p(z,b), without changing any coefficient.

Every core fiber has support 2L(t)/3 in each l_i. For t sufficiently
close to t0 this is strictly below 2 (it suffices that L<3).
The unchanged regular support is 2rho/3<4/3<2. Every off-target
isolator is at least one. Therefore all cross-group traces remain
strictly empty, including regular caps on the deformed core.

It follows exactly that:

* each core cap has mass Bcore_new<B;
* each regular cap has its original mass B;
* the group at each regular fiber covers that whole fiber;
* the core group covers all three core fiber spaces at b=0.

This covers the actual mixed source. No assertion of whole-ambient
coverage by the isolated groups is needed. Strict private witnesses
persist: regular vertices are unchanged, and the three vertices of
L K remain in L D_t with the same canonical margin signs. Thus all
3(2^n-1) original caps remain essential on the new source.

This transfer is even simpler than the shared-plane one-fiber mode
criterion: all original planes stay fixed and three source fibers
move together. It does not follow by independently perturbing the
three fibers, and no preliminary radial strictification is required.

## 3. Matching certificates for the new true maximum

Let

    M_n=M0+Nreg B/Gamma,
    delta(t)=Mcore_new-M0>0.

The retained cover proves that every new source point has absolute
mixed depth at most B. A centroid of any unchanged regular simplex
has absolute depth at least its own-fiber ordinary depth B, for
every closed ambient halfspace containing it. There is such a
regular fiber because n>=2. Thus

    max_y A_mu_new(y)=B,
    max_y depth_mu_new(y)=B/(M_n+delta(t))
                         < B/M_n.                    (4)

The upper bound applies to all deterministic source points, not
only the old maximizing centers. The lower bound handles all
oblique and vertical caps. No claim about unlisted individual
cap masses is required: the unchanged finite cover controls the
infimum defining depth, and a regular centroid supplies equality.

If fixed total mass is desired, apply one common continuous scaling
x -> a(t)x with a(t)^2=M_n/(M_n+delta(t)). Transform each retained
plane along with the source; its base threshold is multiplied by
a(t). This preserves the integer lattice and all source incidences.
The new total mass is exactly M_n and every selected absolute cap
budget is now STRICTLY below B, including regular caps. The exact
absolute maximum is a(t)^2 B, and normalized depth is still (4).

## 4. An exact finite rational deformation

Choose t=9/100 and L=1007/1000 instead of the square-root path (2).
All vertices are rational and the exact core quantities are

    Mcore_new=16826115057/10000000000,
    delta=26115057/10000000000 > 0,
    Bcore_new=2271685752437/2975700000000,
    B-Bcore_new=892421526211/883782900000000 > 0.        (5)

Since 2L/3<2, all isolation and essentiality arguments apply with
no asymptotic qualification. For every n>=2 the new normalized
maximum is exactly

    Gamma/[2^n-4978/4865 + Gamma delta/B].              (6)

It is strictly smaller than the original value. It is still above
Gamma/2^n, as follows from Mcore_new<2B/Gamma=6811/1980.
Thus this is a strict variational descent at a source with an exact
near-target global budget, not a violation of the OC target.

The endpoint motion is nonradial about zero: the vertex with
x-coordinate 2/3 fixes any proposed homothety factor, while its
y-coordinate -1/3+t changes with t. The finite radial obstruction
is therefore consistent with this path.

## 5. Verification scope

../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_binary_critical_nonradial_depth_descent.py uses exact rational
polygon hulls and clipping for the core, checks (5), tests additional
rational near paths with q from (2), verifies binary isolation for
n=2,...,7, and checks the matching depth and normalization formulas.
The proof above establishes all n>=2 and the full smooth local path.

## 6. A fixed isolated-cover mass ceiling

There is a simple limitation on this entire isolated-cover mechanism.
Suppose the same groups still isolate their assigned sources, cover
those sources, and have individual cap masses at most B. Allow any
actual convex replacement of each regular fiber, and any compatible
replacement of the three core fibers. At an ordinary deepest point
of a regular fiber, its assigned three-cap cover and ordinary
Grunbaum imply Gamma times the fiber volume is at most B. Thus
each regular fiber has volume at most B/Gamma. The three core caps
cover the core source, so their mass sum bounds its mass by 3B.
Consequently

    M <= (2^n-2)B/Gamma+3B
       = (2^n-2/3)B/Gamma < 2^n B/Gamma.               (7)

In particular this isolated cover can never attain a uniform budget
B below the target Gamma M/2^n, regardless of any nonradial source
variation within these hypotheses. When B is also the true absolute
maximum, as it is along our deformation, (7) directly proves the
source remains OC-safe. For arbitrary replacements, an upper cap
budget B alone is not a matching lower depth certificate; (7) should
then be read as an obstruction to a subtarget budget for this cover.
The asymptotic nearness of the example supplies no global closure.
